ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-EYE-004: Sky Colour Reflection Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Two 10 ohm resistors in parallel. Total resistance?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Equivalent resistance is 10 + 10 = 20 ohms because adding resistors always increases R.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-005: Parallel Resistance Addition Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Adding parallel resistor across circuit. R_eq change?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Total resistance increases because you add more resistive obstruction.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-005: Parallel Resistance Addition Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: 60W and 100W bulbs in parallel. Which glows brighter?
ordered_attempts.student_response: 60W bulb glows brighter because higher resistance creates more heat by P = I^2*R.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

ordered_attempts.stem: R1 < R2 in parallel across constant V. Which dissipates more heat?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Larger R2 produces more heat because P = I^2*R means heat is proportional to R.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

ordered_attempts.stem: Can two magnetic field lines cross each other?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Yes, field lines cross where the magnetic field is very strong.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-004: Field Line Crossing Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Diagram shows two field lines intersecting at point P. Valid?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Lines intersect at the neutral point between opposing magnetic poles.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-004: Field Line Crossing Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Stationary electron near North pole. Magnetic force?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Electron is strongly attracted because North pole is like a positive charge (+Q).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Equivalence Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Does static magnet pull at-rest charges?
ordered_attempts.student_response: North pole pulls negative charges by electrostatic attraction.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Equivalence Fallacy

topic: Force & Laws of Motion: Newton's Third Law

ordered_attempts.stem: Horse pulls cart, cart pulls horse. Why does system move?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Forces cancel out to zero on cart, so horse must produce force greater than reaction.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-FOR-002: Action-Reaction Self-Cancellation Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: If action equals reaction, why do objects accelerate?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Third law only applies when objects are stationary; moving action beats reaction.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-FOR-002: Action-Reaction Self-Cancellation Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: Lower half of convex lens covered with black paper. What happens to projected image?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The top half of the candle image is completely missing because the bottom half is covered.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-OPT-001: Half-Lens Blocking Fallacy

ordered_attempts.stem: PhET simulation: Observe virtual mask covering lower half of lens.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Wait, the full image is still formed on the screen, just dimmer! Every point on lens receives light from entire object.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: COGNITIVE_CONFLICT_RECONCILED: Full image persists with 50% brightness

ordered_attempts.stem: Near-transfer isomorphic question: cover top 30% of lens.
ordered_attempts.student_response: The complete image remains on screen, but brightness is 70% of original.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response

ordered_attempts.stem: Two identical bulbs in series with 6V battery. Compare ammeters.
ordered_attempts.student_response: A1 = 1.2A, A2 = 0.8A, A3 = 0.4A because bulb 1 consumes electric current.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-001: Current Attenuation / Consumption Model

ordered_attempts.stem: PhET Simulation: Observe moving electron dots and ammeters in series.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Both ammeters read identical values (0.90A)! Current is not consumed; only electrical potential energy drops.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: COGNITIVE_CONFLICT_RECONCILED: Current is conserved in closed loop

ordered_attempts.stem: Near-transfer isomorphic question: 100-ohm and 20-ohm resistors in series.
ordered_attempts.student_response: I_in = I_out, because in any series circuit electric charge cannot accumulate or vanish.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response

ordered_attempts.stem: Runner covers 100 m in 5 s. Speed?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Speed = distance / time = 100 / 5 = 25 m/s (mental arithmetic slip on division).
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CARELESS_CALCULATION_ERROR

ordered_attempts.stem: Car travels 300 m in 15 s. Speed?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Average speed is distance divided by elapsed time: 300 / 15 = 20 m/s.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: CORRECT: Scientifically Accurate Response
